transcript: Interview Guide. Activity E. FGD:  Aspirations of Youth
Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)

(When we just started this activity, the elder women of the community were very concerned if what we are going to ask by this young group. But we tried to control the situation by allowing their long sitting and somehow by joining the discussion. Even we were left alone with the group but some of the elder women of the house/family and village kept on having multiple visits to the room where we were conducting the activity. We also included one married young female so the atmosphere somehow became light. Because there was a kind of doubt in their minds that perhaps we were going to ask something very confidential and something that is not possible be asked/discuss in presence of elder women, mothers and aunts etc.)

(We tried at our optimum level to carry out this activity in private with each of the FGD participant- ladder of power and freedom. Unfortunately the majority of the responses were same. In spite of not stressing on individual case, rather asking about the generalized situation of the women’s decision making power, they each time gave examples of their mothers first and then exemplified their own decision making position in their lives.)

(They put majority of women on the second (2) step of the ladder with very little power and say. However, some rare cases in the tenant community as well as in the land owner families do exist whom they put on the fifth (5) step in the ladder with optimum power and freedom in making certain decisions. But this is interesting to know that these women were elderly women, who were having this power and freedom in making decision regarding others’ lives i.e. their daughters, sons, and even what to purchase/sell etc. And this is again important to know that when these women were young so they had no power and freedom for making any decisions even about their own lives.)
(Six members put themselves on the 2nd step of the ladder while two thought themselves on 3rd step. )
“We are young; they are elder so men make decisions”-XX

When asked by XX what about your mother, aunts sisters etc? Do they have the right to make any decisions by own… “No, they are also not allowed, they are told to observe ‘Purdah’ veil” and she laughed. (hahaha)

“May be our men think higher education of female as something bad/ challenging for an existing normative gender pattern. Saying XX and endorsed by others.

Yes. At lease this we can answer that now new technologies like thrasher, grass cutter/fodder preparation cutter and tractors have eased the human labor and shortened the time consumption. Actually the cause is just the spread of these technologies by observing and discussion of male with other farmers/land lords.

In tenants’ families these things really don’t matter and whatever they do, they (men and women, young and old) all do it together. However, for us this really matter. Our men never allow us to go and work outside be that on the family forms/off the family forms/any other job for cash. And this is very true in our case that certain gender costumes all the way govern women’s lives and action here.

Normally here the lands are on share bases. For instance, brothers/cousins/uncles have their shared lands. In such cases an individual may not make certain choice/decisions by his own. However, in cases where an individual has his single/separate land so there such choices can be made. There are some modal where some individuals tried some new vegetable varies for the first time.

In women’s case this is almost impossible. Yes those who raise livestock at their houses can sell some of the livestock products such as dairy or poultry stuff like milk, eggs, and yogurt but generally speaking people here in our community don’t actually do so. Yes in tenants’ community women do sell their livestock products mostly to us. One thing that we always buy from them “Bhaanrrh/Khaad” animals’ dung/manure as we use it as a source of burning/cooking.

The only thing which matter is that women do not have certain choices/say for making such decisions what and where to cultivate, or who owns hat plots. Other like the proximity to house, soil quality, size or irrigation sources as such do not matter. Men own property, land, crops and all decisions regarding this all stuff.
Women even as wives don’t get any spate share of husband’s property. All land is owned by men.

àWhen Probed further, if women have their due share in the family property or not. So the answer was that women do not get share in the father’s/family property/lands. The only portion they get is the share in the farm products i.e. wheat, maize, rice for family consumption based on the needs. Further probed if unmarried and married women both can get any land share or not? Again the same answer that women in both cases do not get any share. Only one case was pointed out in which the woman’s husband was died so she asked her brothers to give her land share so her sons can cultivate it by themself. Eventually she got her share in the family land but again gave it to her sons for cultivation. But at least she could get her share whether because of her very poor economic status.

Since, women don’t possess land and property so they are not in a situation to make certain choices, but in case if they are given a choice to do so, they will consult their men in the family i.e. husband, brother, father, son or son in law etc.

Male consult other male farmers, friends, relatives and those who have good farms obviously. Very few elderly women/mothers are however consulted and discussed by the sons what they are going to cultivate and why. Male never consult their wives for certain matters. Because they think that women lack essential knowledge and experiences in this respect.
